status: Two style trials for user selection; not a production deck.

prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: a trial playing-card face for a premium minimalist digital poker game.
Primary request: ONE King of Spades card in a distinctive geometric modernist style, minimal but interesting, suitable for developing a coherent 52-card deck.
Composition: straight-on orthographic flat card face, portrait poker-card proportions approximately 5:7. Show the entire single ivory-white card with subtly rounded corners, centred with a very narrow light grey outer margin. The card fills almost all of the image. No perspective, mockup devices, table, hands, packaging, or extra cards.
Artwork: a double-ended crowned king constructed from a very few confident black geometric shapes, architectural arches, semicircles and fine negative-space cuts. A quiet sculptural silhouette: abstract but recognisably a king in profile, mirrored rotationally at the waist like a real court card. Subtle spade geometry woven into the crown and torso. The illustration occupies the central 50 percent of the face, with generous unprinted space around it. At most one hairline rule integrated into the artwork, no surrounding decorative frame.
Typography and gameplay: an extremely legible 'K' above an accurate solid black spade symbol in the upper-left corner. An identical K-and-spade index rotated 180 degrees in the lower-right corner. Both indices inset evenly from edges, large enough to identify on a small phone. No other text. All suit symbols must be spades, never clubs or hearts.
Palette: black ink and warm white only. Crisp edges, nearly flat ink, faint natural paper character at most. No metallic ink, no gradient, no colour.
Mood: restrained designer stationery, an original collectible deck with strong visual identity. It must be simpler and more elegant than a traditional ornate court card, but substantially more designed than a single giant suit symbol.
Avoid: ornate engraving, busy patterns, photoreal people, three-dimensional sculpture, bevels, drop shadows, fantasy art, baroque borders, gold, watermarks, labels.

Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: a trial playing-card face for a premium minimalist digital poker game.
Primary request: ONE Queen of Hearts card in a distinctive flowing monoline illustration style, minimal but interesting, suitable for developing a coherent 52-card deck.
Composition: straight-on orthographic flat card face, portrait poker-card proportions approximately 5:7. Show the entire single ivory-white card with subtly rounded corners, centred with a very narrow light grey outer margin. The card fills almost all the image. No perspective, devices, hands, table, packaging or additional cards.
Artwork: an original airy double-ended queen drawn with a small number of graceful black continuous contour lines. Recognisable crowned face in profile, a simple arc of hair and a single heart-shaped flourish in the central composition. Mirror the queen rotationally at the waist like a real court card. Lines feel deliberate and sensual, almost a modern calligraphic fashion drawing, with plenty of negative space. Use only a few open curves and one or two tiny solid black accents. Central artwork covers roughly half the card width and 60 percent of its height. The queen's silhouette should read at small size without fine decorative detail. No decorative border.
Typography and gameplay: a highly legible refined 'Q' above an unmistakable filled heart symbol in upper-left. An identical Q-and-heart index rotated 180 degrees in lower-right. Corner indices inset evenly from edges and clearly readable on a phone. All suit symbols are hearts. No other lettering.
Palette: black ink on warm white, strictly monochrome. Sharp clean graphic edges, no grey shading, very faint paper character at most.
Mood: quiet luxury through drawing and negative space. A clear stylistic alternative to solid geometric playing-card art; expressive and human but edited down to essentials.
Avoid: dense engraving, elaborate Art Nouveau vines, traditional multicolour royal clothing, photoreal portraits, gradients, gold, neon, realistic 3D, heavy black blocks, watermarks, labels.
